The Vampire's Coffin (1958) - IMDb

I wish the swinging pendulum hypnosis trope weren't so common: it's dumb and so is this movie. Don't bother to turn on subtitles: there is nothing in the story you can't glean from the onscreen action. Even for a 1950s era horror film, this is so campy I don't see why they didn't just make a comedy like Abbott and Costello Meet Count Lavud. The cinematography, lighting, sets, and special effects are all bad. The acting is barely passable, with the exception of Germán Robles whom I hadn't seen before. Robles is quite compelling as the demonic villain, and conveys about as much presence as anyone who isn't the great Bela Lugosi possibly could.

Score: 1/5
